intro: Hindu families keep many festivals. Two big ones are Diwali and Holi. Diwali is the festival of lights. Holi is the festival of colors.
Festivals come with stories. The stories often teach values. You will learn namaste, ahimsa and seva. All children can talk about these ideas.
By the end, you can say how families get ready for Diwali. You can tell about Holi and Prahlada. You can name ways to be kind.
bigQuestion: How do festivals and stories help people be kind?

timeline.t: In autumn, a family cleans the house for Diwali
Children make a rangoli pattern by the door
The family lights little clay diyas
Many families do a Lakshmi puja and share sweets
In spring, people light a bonfire the night before Holi
Friends throw colored powder and make up
People greet each other with namaste
Neighbors do seva and help each other

words.d: the festival of lights in the autumn
a small clay lamp with oil and a wick
a colorful pattern made on the floor with powder, rice or petals
a time of worship, with offerings like flowers and lamps
a greeting with hands pressed together and a small bow
helping others without asking for anything back

test.q: Which festival is the festival of lights?
test.why: Diwali is the festival of lights.

test.q: Which festival is the festival of colors?
test.why: Holi is the festival of colors.
A diya is a small clay lamp.
Rangoli by the door welcomes guests.

test.q: Who do many families honor on Diwali night?
test.why: Many families do a Lakshmi puja on Diwali.

test.q: Which faiths keep Diwali besides Hindus?
test.why: Sikhs and Jains keep Diwali too.

test.q: Who is the brave boy in the Holi story?
test.why: Prahlada is the brave boy in the Holi story.
Namaste is a greeting with hands pressed together.
Seva means helping others without asking for anything back.

write.prompt: Draw and tell. Pick Diwali or Holi. Draw one thing families do. Tell a grown-up what they do and what many families say it means.
tips: Say "Many families say..." when you tell what it means.
Use a word from this unit, like diya, rangoli or seva.
